does: Fries pine nuts or blanched almonds in a little hot oil or ghee, stirring, until they turn an even gold, then lifts them out to drain. They are scattered over rice and meat at the end for crunch.
how: Use a small pan and a thin layer of oil, ghee or butter.
Heat it over a medium heat and add the nuts in one layer.
Stir all the time, since nuts colour unevenly and fast.
Lift them out a shade paler than you want them, since they keep darkening off the heat.

cues.text: An even gold, with no dark brown nuts.
A rich, toasty smell. Bitterness means they have gone too far.

mistakes.mistake: Walking away from the pan, so that the nuts burn in the last moments.
mistakes.fix: Stay by the pan and stir.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the fried nuts in the hot pan, so that they keep darkening.

variant_of.differs: The nuts are fried in a little fat rather than browned in a dry pan, which makes them richer and more evenly gold.
